examples.question: Condition prevalence for diabetes
examples.answer: 8 distinct coded condition groups returned. Each group's prevalence is shown separately; patients can appear in multiple groups, so the counts must not be added together. citations.title: Recorded condition prevalence
citations.definition: Distinct patients with a confirmed active, recurrent, or relapsed condition divided by all loaded patients, grouped by terminology system and code. An optional filter matches the condition name.
limitations: This is a current recorded snapshot, not historical population prevalence.
The denominator includes all loaded patients, including deceased patients.
Unknown verification, refuted, error, and inactive conditions are excluded.
Name filters are literal substring matches, not clinical concept sets; condition groups can overlap.

FHIR Condition resources may describe social context, history, and care situations as well as clinical conditions; this metric includes them and does not identify chronic disease. Dashboard groups are a separate curated presentation mapping.
